title: Falsy config file values silently dropped
description: In base.py:83, `if dict_value:` skips falsy values (0, False, empty string, empty list/dict) loaded from config files. A config file with `debug: false` or `count: 0` will have those values silently ignored, falling back to class defaults instead.
acceptance: Change `if dict_value:` to `if dict_value is not None:` or `if member in self._current_dict` so that falsy values from config files are correctly applied. Add tests for falsy config file values (0, False, empty string, empty list).

acceptance.new: Change `if dict_value:` to `if dict_value is not None:` or `if member in self._current_dict` so that falsy values from config files are correctly applied. Add tests for falsy config file values (0, False, empty string, empty list).

acceptance: In strict mode, raise ValueError for unrecognized bool strings (anything not in the true set AND not in an explicit false set like {'false', '0', 'no', 'n'}). Update the docstring to list all accepted values.

  - Environment variable: APP_DB_USER

Shallow generic type checking in strict mode
description: In base.py:100-111, _strict mode checks origin types only (e.g. list) but not element types (e.g. list[str] accepts [1, 2, 3]). This is undocumented and could mislead users who expect full generic validation.
acceptance: Either: (a) document this as 'origin-only' checking in the docstring and README, or (b) implement deeper element type validation. At minimum, update the _strict docstring to clarify the limitation.

dir(self) introspection is expensive and fragile
description: In base.py:124, _get_members() uses dir(self) which walks the entire MRO including inherited methods, then filters out properties and private members. This is O(n) over all attributes and fragile if someone adds descriptors. It runs on every instantiation.
acceptance: Replace dir(self) with vars(self.__class__) + get_type_hints() to avoid the full MRO walk. Alternatively, cache the result at the class level since the members don't change between instances. All existing tests must pass.

acceptance: Allow _prefix to be overridden via __init__ parameter (e.g. BaseConfig(prefix='custom')). The class-level default should still work for backwards compatibility. Add tests for runtime prefix override.
